answer: Each agent gets a persistent signing key, but a key alone earns no influence: to enter the market’s reputation-weighted order book, it must lock a scarce deposit and pay a small fee on each trade. Validators slash the deposit when signed deals are proven fraudulent, while honest history gradually improves access. An attacker can mint keys cheaply, but cannot cheaply give each one credible trading history: every fake identity ties up capital, pays fees, and risks losing its stake. A cedar seller, a ferrous broker, and a river hauler all face the same cost.
